task: Sweep the clock-tree configuration (ClockTree->NumberLevels, RowClockFanout) to find the minimum-delay setting per buffer size. No permanent source changes to BroadcastHTree (Sweep 3's required_transition edits were temporary, restored and diff-verified).

sweep_1_number_levels.description: NumberLevels = 1..ceil(log2(N)) plus auto, at RowClockFanout = 0 and 4, for all 4 (N,B) points.
sweep_1_number_levels.headline_finding: NumberLevels=1 minimizes t_write_clock_path at EVERY (N,B) point, at BOTH fanout=0 and fanout=4 -- not ceil(log2(N)) (the current auto default) and not ceil(log2(N)/2) (the log4 hypothesis this task offered). For N=4, ceil(log2(N)/2)=1 happens to coincide with the true optimum, but for N=64 (ceil(log2(N)/2)=3) and N=512 (ceil(log2(N)/2)=5), the true optimum (1) undershoots even the log4 hypothesis. The honest characterization is 'as few tree levels as structurally possible' (levels=1), not a fanout-4-derived formula. Delay increases monotonically-ish with levels beyond 1 (with a non-monotonic jump-then-plateau around levels 6-9 at N=512, likely a repeater-insertion-algorithm segment-count step effect, not independently diagnosed further -- out of this task's scope).

sweep_2_row_clock_fanout.description: RowClockFanout = 0, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 at NumberLevels=1 (the Sweep 1 delay-minimizer) for all 4 (N,B) points.
sweep_2_row_clock_fanout.headline_finding: RowClockFanout=0 (no RowBuf chain at all -- direct connection) minimizes t_write_clock_path at EVERY point, consistent with the prior task's finding that adding the fanout-4 BUF chain made delay WORSE, not better, at the two points tested there. Here, across the full 0/2/3/4/6/8 sweep, delay is worst at fanout=2 and generally improves (decreases) as fanout rises from 2 toward 8, but never beats fanout=0 (no buffering) at any point tested.

sweep_3_sizing_target_sensitivity.description: required_transition temporarily set to 20e-12 and 10e-12 (from the current 40e-12), rebuilt, measured at the Sweep 1-2 best settings (levels=1) across fanout=0..8, at all 4 points. File restored to 40e-12 afterward -- byte-identical diff CONFIRMED.
sweep_3_sizing_target_sensitivity.finding: Tightening the sizing target generally reduces delay further, but not always monotonically or by a large amount: (512,32) and (64,128) improve smoothly and substantially (~20% each from 40ps-best to 10ps-best); (512,256) actually gets WORSE at 20ps before improving again at 10ps (reported as observed, not smoothed over); (4,32) shows NO change across all three targets at all (already at max driving strength / below the target at this tiny scale, so tightening it further has no effect there). The hardcoded 40e-12 constant is NOT the dominant remaining delay source anywhere -- it accounts for 0% to ~21% of the 40ps-best remaining delay across the four points, meaning the majority of the remaining 40-250ps delay comes from fundamental gate/wire RC at the current sizing, not from this specific hardcoded choice. This constant's own TODO (mentioned in the task's context) is a real but secondary lever, confirmed by measurement, not assumed.

1_best_vs_pre_phase4_baseline.description: Best t_write_clock_path per point (NumberLevels=1, RowClockFanout=0, at the CURRENT/unchanged 40ps sizing target -- since Sweep 3's tighter targets are measurement-only, not part of the recommended, deployable setting) vs the pre-Phase-4 unbuffered baseline.
1_best_vs_pre_phase4_baseline.headline: The tree is now FASTER than the pre-Phase-4 unbuffered baseline at EVERY point (1.76x to 4.73x), using only a parameter change (NumberLevels=1, RowClockFanout=0) -- no source modification. This directly resolves the prior task's finding that the tree, at its AUTO/fanout=4 defaults, was actually SLOWER than the unbuffered baseline at (512,256) (0.92x, a regression). That regression is a consequence of the DEFAULT parameter choice, not an inherent limitation of DSENT's tree model -- correcting the parameters resolves it cleanly.

2_area_idle_cost_of_best_setting.description: Area and Idle-energy cost of the best-delay setting (levels=1, fanout=0) versus the CURRENT default (levels=auto, fanout=4).
2_area_idle_cost_of_best_setting.headline: There is NO real tradeoff here: the best-delay setting is simultaneously SMALLER in area (-0.28% to -1.78%) and dramatically LOWER in Idle energy (-89% to -99%) than the current default, at every point. Fewer tree levels and no row-buffer chain simply means fewer cells switching every cycle. The current default (auto levels + fanout=4) is worse than the recommended setting on every axis measured -- delay, area, AND idle energy -- with no offsetting benefit found.

3_refit_depth_scaling.description: t_write_clock_path vs log2(N) at B=32, N=4..512, using the best settings (NumberLevels=1, RowClockFanout=0).

comparison_to_current_default_fit.conclusion: The re-fit IMPROVES both R^2 (0.755 -> 0.883) and, more importantly, reduces the slope by ~6x (7.28e-11 -> 1.24e-11 s per log2-doubling) -- growth with depth is much gentler at the best settings, as expected once the H-tree's own level-count contribution is minimized. It does NOT fully linearize, though: residuals still show curvature (a dip in the middle of the range, N=64-256, and an uptick at the largest N=512), so 'accelerating growth at large N' is reduced but not eliminated -- reported honestly rather than claiming a perfect fix.

4_plausibility_gate.description: Best t_write_clock_path as a percentage of a 1 ns clock period at each point (NumberLevels=1, RowClockFanout=0).
4_plausibility_gate.conclusion: All 4 points are comfortably under the ~30% flag threshold (max 24.50% at (512,256)) -- a credible design point. For contrast, the CURRENT default settings (levels=auto, fanout=4) reach 82.88% of the period at (512,256) -- a value that WOULD have failed this plausibility gate, underscoring that the default parameters (not DSENT's tree model itself) are the source of the previously implausible numbers.

5_default_settings_unperturbed.description: Area, leakage, e_read, e_write at the DEFAULT settings (levels=auto, fanout=4), confirmed unchanged by the sweep (including after Sweep 3's temporary required_transition edits and restoration).
5_default_settings_unperturbed.confirmation: Bit-for-bit identical to the prior task's stored/measured Phase-4-default numbers (e.g. (4,32): area=2.489626e-10 both, e_read=4.277821e-14 both, e_write=1.304276e-13 both) -- the sweep and the temporary Sweep 3 source edits did not perturb the default configuration's results at all.

deliverable_recommendation.recommendation: Hard-set ClockTree->NumberLevels default to 1 (i.e. change the auto formula from 'ceil(log2(NumberEntries))' to a flat '1') and RowClockFanout default to 0 (i.e. disable the per-row BUF chain by default) in DFFRAM.cc.
deliverable_recommendation.justification: Across all 4 measured (N,B) points and the full B=32 depth sweep, NumberLevels=1 and RowClockFanout=0 simultaneously minimize t_write_clock_path, minimize area, AND minimize Idle energy -- there is no tradeoff to weigh; every other tested combination is worse on every axis. At these settings the tree beats the pre-Phase-4 unbuffered baseline at every point (1.76x-4.73x), stays comfortably under the 30% plausibility threshold at every point (max 24.5%), and the depth-scaling fit improves substantially (slope 6x gentler, R^2 up from 0.755 to 0.883). NumberLevels=1 also has an appealing interpretation: it corresponds to the structural minimum this model supports (constructModel() ASSERTs NumberLevels>0), effectively reducing the H-tree to a single repeated-segment stage feeding the leaf driver chain directly -- close to, but not identical to, the true pre-Phase-4 unbuffered design, while still retaining the tree's wire-RC-aware segment-insertion logic for the one level that remains.
deliverable_recommendation.not_applied: This is a recommendation only, per the task's explicit instruction -- DFFRAM.cc has not been modified.
deliverable_recommendation.caveat: This recommendation is based on measurements at the current, unchanged 40e-12 required_transition sizing target. Sweep 3 shows a further, smaller (0-21% of remaining delay, non-monotonic at one point) improvement is available by separately revisiting that hardcoded constant, but that is explicitly out of scope for this task and not folded into this recommendation.

constraints_honored.no_permanent_broadcasthtree_changes: Confirmed via diff after Sweep 3 -- byte-identical to pre-sweep content, required_transition = 40e-12 restored.
constraints_honored.no_dffram_changes: DFFRAM.cc was read-only throughout this task -- only its existing ClockTree->NumberLevels and RowClockFanout parameters were set from the measurement harness, never its source.
constraints_honored.area: Area->Active only, never summed with Metal1Wire
